next_item_hypothesis: One demonstrated failure is that a single flat residual-code geometry can allocate capacity poorly to strongly directional, non-reversible next-item transitions: the train-only manifest records 314605 directed pairs with no observed reverse event (fraction 0.9266197178950221), across 339519 transitions, while mean next-item entropy is 4.844072338042215 bits. This motivates testing whether curved residual quantization improves the first-token grouping of next-item targets; the counts establish asymmetry, not that curvature causes improvement. Stage2 constructs one deterministic global three-token SID per item from content embeddings only and never ranks items. Stage3 T5 is the sole next-item ranker.

math_definition.builder: For each catalog item i, a frozen content encoder produces e_i; a learned shared affine map gives z_i in R^32. The three-level residual quantizer emits k_i1,k_i2,k_i3 in {0,...,255}; the global SID is exactly (k_i1,k_i2,k_i3), independent of user, batch, history, or request. No prefix Transformer, beam search, user bootstrap, ranking loss, Recall/NDCG objective, or recommender component is included in this builder.
math_definition.frozen_training_protocol: Use the existing Stage2 baseline's exact epochs (3000), batch size, schedule, seeds, optimizer, data split, and codebook initialization, without sweep or early stopping. Keep architecture, parameter count, initialization, optimizer, schedule, seeds, training budget, and every non-geometry setting identical between arms. The geometry parameter is the sole arm difference. The flat arm is the c->0 evaluation of the same implementation. Any graph-signal arm, if separately instantiated, receives that same graph signal during training in both geometries; this proposal itself adds no graph arm.
math_definition.constants_and_domain: Curvature c=1.0 for the curved arm and c->0 for the flat arm; temperature tau=0.1; epsilon=1e-5; stable arcosh(u)=log1p((u-1)+sqrt((u-1)*(u+1))) for u>=1, with u clamped from below to 1 before evaluation. For numerical roundoff, squared norms in denominators are clamped so each factor is at least epsilon. Every vector entering any scored distance in either arm is projected to the same closed ball of fixed radius R=0.99 (<1): P_R(v)=v*min(1,R/max(||v||,tiny)), with tiny=1e-12. This common bounded feasible region and representation map apply in both arms.
math_definition.scored_distance: For projected x,y in R^32, the sole scored power is squared distance D^2(x,y)=d_c(x,y)^2=(1/c)*arcosh(1+2c*||x-y||^2/((1-c*||x||^2)*(1-c*||y||^2)))^2. Its exact c->0 limit is 4*||x-y||^2; the unsquared distance tends to 2*||x-y||. All assignment and reconstruction scoring uses this same squared power in both arms.
math_definition.c_dependent_maps_and_flat_limit: The origin exponential map is exp^c_0(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)*||v||/2)*v/(sqrt(c)*||v||), with its continuous value 0 at v=0; its c->0 limit is v (identity). The projection radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c) is undefined at c=0 and is not used: both arms instead use the common fixed R=0.99 projection P_R above. Thus no c-dependent radius is evaluated at zero. The scored distance has the exact flat limit stated above. These are all c-dependent rules in this specification.
math_definition.residual_assignment_order: At level l=1,2,3, take the current tangent residual r_i,l in R^32 (r_i,1=z_i). Apply map u_i,l=exp^c_0(r_i,l), then project x_i,l=P_R(u_i,l). For each code j, project its unconstrained code vector q_j,l by y_j,l=P_R(exp^c_0(q_j,l)); assign k_i,l=argmin_j D^2(x_i,l,y_j,l), breaking ties by smallest code index. Only after assignment, subtract in tangent coordinates: r_i,l+1=r_i,l-q_k_i,l,l, where q_k is the learned unconstrained tangent code parameter. The residual subtraction is not projected; before the next level it is mapped, then projected, then assigned, then subtracted in that exact order. Any residual update scored at the current or a subsequent level is always map -> project -> assign -> subtract; no post-subtraction projection is allowed. After three levels, reconstruction is formed from the sum of the three tangent code vectors, mapped and projected before its distance is scored.
math_definition.reconstruction_loss: Named tensors: Z=(z_i)_{i in I}, Q=(q_j,l)_{l=1..3,j=0..255}, assignments K=(k_i,l), projected latent X_i=P_R(exp^c_0(z_i)), and projected reconstruction Y_i=P_R(exp^c_0(sum_l q_k_i,l,l)); all vectors are 32-dimensional and i ranges over training-split catalog items I with content embeddings. L_rec=(1/|I|) sum_{i in I} D^2(X_i,Y_i). Reduction is a uniform item mean; I is nonempty by construction, otherwise the run is invalid (no zero substitute). Assignments are stop-gradient argmin outputs. The target Y depends on learned code parameters; gradients flow through selected q vectors and the encoder/map, but assignments are treated as constants for this reconstruction update, preventing target/assignment circular gradients.
math_definition.commitment_loss: For each i in I and level l, let X_i,l=P_R(exp^c_0(r_i,l)) and C_i,l=P_R(exp^c_0(q_k_i,l,l)), both shape [32]. L_com=(1/(3|I|)) sum_{i in I,l in {1,2,3}} D^2(stopgrad(X_i,l), C_i,l). It is a uniform mean over item-level pairs; empty I is invalid. The encoder/residual target is detached while gradients update selected code parameters through C; assignment indices are detached argmins, so no parameter-dependent discrete target is differentiated. Together optimize L_rec+L_com with the frozen baseline's unchanged training protocol and loss weighting; no additional loss is introduced.
math_definition.transition_target_distribution: Allowed train-only signal uses observed training transitions (a,b) with counts n_ab. Let frozen hard assignments Kbar be obtained by the same content-only builder at the start of each epoch and detached for the entire epoch. For target item b, let p2(b)=(kbar_b1,kbar_b2). Define m_{p,k}=sum_{(a,b) in T_train} 1[p2(b)=p]1[kbar_b3=k], m_p=sum_k m_{p,k}, and h_{a,k}=sum_{b:(a,b) in T_train}1[kbar_b3=k], h_a=sum_k h_{a,k}. Then for each observed train pair (a,b), q_{ab,k}=0.5*(h_{a,k}+1)/(h_a+256)+0.5*(m_{p2(b),k}+1)/(m_{p2(b)}+256), k=0..255. Each factor sums to one; q has shape [|T_train|,256]. This is the only behavior auxiliary target; its transition counts and detached prefix assignments are fixed within the epoch, so no target depends differentiably on the parameters it supervises. Empty transition set disables this auxiliary term for that epoch (not applicable to the stated train data); no normalization by an empty group is performed. The auxiliary term is used only if included as an explicitly common graph/signal comparison; this candidate's frozen objective contains only reconstruction and commitment losses, so q is diagnostic supervision definition and not an extra training loss.
math_definition.conditioning: The L3 prefix prior conditions exactly on the earlier pair (k1,k2), and on no other code or context. For diagnostic conditional G3, the history term is the anchor item's train-transition L3-code distribution Laplace-smoothed with alpha=1 over 256 codes; the prefix term is the target's train-transition L3-code distribution conditioned exactly on its L2 prefix (k1,k2), also Laplace-smoothed with alpha=1 over 256 codes. Validation pairs are scored only after fitting; they never enter training, assignments-as-targets, counts, or parameter updates.

hyperbolic_necessity: Negative curvature is a falsifiable inductive bias for directional transition structure: a hierarchy of increasingly specific residual codes may represent broad item neighborhoods and their branching refinements with less distortion than a flat metric, while the observed lack of reverse transitions suggests that symmetric proximity alone may not organize target-side refinements adequately. The proposed mechanism is specifically curved squared-distance residual VQ, not a claim that asymmetry mathematically entails hyperbolicity. Curvature is necessary for this candidate's hypothesis only if the matched flat-limit arm fails to reproduce the registered improvements under identical representation domain and protocol.
euclidean_control: The control is the identical implementation with c->0: same content vectors, trainable maps and code vectors, three-level assignment and residual subtraction, shared fixed projection P_R, squared-distance objective, parameter count, initialization, codebook initialization, optimizer, schedule, seeds, epochs, batch, and budget. Only the distance formula changes to its exact flat limit 4*||x-y||^2; exp map becomes identity. It does not remove or alter projection, data, training signal, architecture, or diagnostics.
effect_site: Expected Stage2 diagnostics: valid L1 positive hit rate increases; valid Hard-L1 ER increases; level2_distinct_prefixes increases; L3 collision decreases; L3 refinement gain increases; conditional G3 increases. These are diagnostic predictions, not assumed outcomes or substitutes for Stage3 behavior.
real_trigger_measurement: The single trigger is train-only directed item-transition asymmetry: among distinct directed item pairs observed in the training-split longest-prefix-per-user population, count pairs with no observed reverse. The frozen measured value is 314605 of 323633 (0.9266197178950221). This selects the demonstrated failure hypothesis only; validation/test behavior, future events, and prediction-time user context are excluded.
training_only_inputs: Stage2 learns content embedding to SID from frozen item content and legal train-split item transitions only if a common train signal is needed; this specified candidate's optimization uses content-only reconstruction and commitment. No validation/test behavior, future event, validation pair, prediction-time user context, validation-derived target, or batch-composition-dependent assignment is permitted. Frozen validation pairs are read only for the registered diagnostics and Stage3 validation protocol; test is read only for the registered Stage3 outcome.

stage2_diagnostics.name: valid_L1_positive_hit_rate
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Compute per matched frozen training seed on the exact 52855 validation pairs (one positive and ten negatives per anchor, seed 42, history[-1] -> target); compare paired curved-flat differences, then arithmetic-mean across the frozen matched training seeds.

stage2_diagnostics.name: valid_Hard_L1_ER
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Use 10*positive_hits/negative_hits with negative hits counted over the same ten negatives; evaluate each matched seed on those same pairs, then arithmetic-mean paired differences. Resample reference is 16.38953942232631.

stage2_diagnostics.name: level2_distinct_prefixes
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Count distinct (k1,k2) over all catalog items per matched seed; arithmetic-mean paired differences.

stage2_diagnostics.name: L3_collision
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Share of all catalog items whose full three-code tuple is shared with another item, per matched seed; arithmetic-mean paired differences.

stage2_diagnostics.name: L3_refinement_gain
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Mean over all catalog items of log2(|bucket(k1,k2)|/|bucket(k1,k2,k3)|), per matched seed; arithmetic-mean paired differences.

stage2_diagnostics.name: conditional_G3
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Mean on the frozen validation pairs of log2(p_hist(L3 target|anchor)/p_pref(L3 target|target prefix2)); prefix prior mixes the train-transition history term with the Laplace-smoothed alpha=1 per-256-code prefix prior; arithmetic-mean paired differences.

stage3_behavioral_test.seed_rule: Train/evaluate Stage3 with the unchanged frozen T5 protocol and same matched seed set and data; compare paired test_R@10 differences, arithmetic-mean across seeds. Test is opened only for this registered final comparison, never for Stage2 selection or tuning.

classification.falsified_if: all registered comparisons are defined and finite, and (stage3_behavioral_test.mean_difference < stage3_behavioral_test.minimum_effect OR every registered stage2_diagnostics entry fails its registered direction/minimum_effect condition)
classification.passed_if: all registered comparisons are defined and finite, and stage3_behavioral_test.mean_difference >= stage3_behavioral_test.minimum_effect and at least one registered stage2_diagnostics entry satisfies its registered direction/minimum_effect condition
classification.mixed_if: all registered comparisons are defined and finite, and neither falsified_if nor passed_if is true

falsifier.null_outcome_rule: If any seed-wise or aggregated change is undefined or non-finite (including zero denominator, missing evaluation, or empty stratum), classify the affected comparison NULL; any comparison containing a NULL seed is inconclusive, neither passed nor falsified. Do not replace NULL with zero, omit a seed, or classify an overall result as passed/falsified when a required comparison is NULL.
